steps.ask: For the log of an inside expression, what two parts do you multiply together?
steps.title: Differentiate the logarithm using the chain rule

lines.text: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln u = \hl{1}{\dfrac{1}{u}}\cdot\hl{2}{\dfrac{du}{dx}}$ with $u = 2x+3$, so $\hl{2}{\dfrac{du}{dx}} = 2$. The constant $C$ differentiates to 0.

problems.note: The inside is now t², not a linear expression, so the reciprocal is 1/t² and the inside derivative is 2t. The same two parts are multiplied, then a common factor of t cancels.

lines.text: For $\ln u$ with $u=t^2$: $\frac{d}{dt}\ln u = \hl{1}{\frac{1}{u}}\cdot\hl{2}{\frac{du}{dt}}$, and $\hl{2}{\frac{du}{dt}}=2t$.

steps.ask: Is there a common factor of t on the top and the bottom?
steps.title: Cancel a factor of t

problems.note: The function is now P(t) = 0.82 − 0.12 ln(t+1): a constant and a coefficient in front of the log. The derivative uses the same rule, then you substitute t = 1 and interpret the sign of the answer.

steps.ask: Differentiate each term of P(t). What does the constant 0.82 become?
steps.title: Differentiate P(t)

lines.text: The derivative of $\ln(t+1)$ is $\hl{1}{\frac{1}{t+1}}$, and the constant $0.82$ differentiates to $0$.

steps.ask: Put t = 1 into your derivative. What is t + 1 when t = 1?
steps.title: Substitute t = 1 into P'(t)

steps.ask: What does a negative rate of change tell you about the proportion as time goes on?
steps.title: Interpret the sign of P'(t) in part (ii)

lines.text: $P'(t)$ is the rate of change of the proportion recalled. It is negative, so $P$ is decreasing.
The proportion of digits recalled correctly decreases as the time $t$ increases.

problems.final: P'(1) = -0.06;\ \text{the proportion recalled decreases over time}
